code-jade.purpose: Inline code literal pills - the deep jade end of the accent family.

display.purpose: Page h1 - friendly geometric sans, weight-led hierarchy.

title.purpose: Card h2 and the brand line.

body.purpose: All UI prose; leads capped near 62 characters per line.

label.purpose: Field labels, buttons, step names - Atkinson Hyperlegible, never uppercase, never small.

helper.purpose: The line under a field that explains what will happen.

mono.purpose: Machine channels only: module codes, identifiers, lab readouts.

shadows.name: ambient-seat
shadows.purpose: Default seat under every card and stat tile.

shadows.name: pop-lift
shadows.purpose: Foreground chrome only - toasts and the nav island.

shadows.name: press-pool
shadows.purpose: The primary button's own colored pool; pairs with an inset top lip rgba(255,255,255,0.28).

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default UI easing (--ease) - a soft spring for a calm, unhurried feel.

motion.name: ease-io
motion.purpose: Continuous states - the breathing camera-status dot, toast exits.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: The one perpetual micro-loop: the status dot that says the sensor is live.

motion.name: panel-in
motion.purpose: State-change entrances: wizard steps (400ms), verdict card and results (300ms).

motion.name: row-in
motion.purpose: Console rows and score rows appearing in sequence.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.purpose: The YOU'RE IN / THAT WASN'T YOU stamp - the system's single loudest moment.

motion.name: toast-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric toast path: bottom-right enters, bottom-right leaves.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.purpose: First-paint choreography via motion.js IntersectionObserver; JS-applied so a failure never hides content.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Large pill CTA in Friendly Teal; the label always says what happens.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 56px; padding: 14px 26px; border: 1px solid #0f9d8c; border-radius: 20px; background: #0f9d8c; color: #ffffff; font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", sans-serif; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 10px 26px -14px rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.7), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.28); transition: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), background 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0b7c6e; border-color: #0b7c6e; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0) scale(0.985); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.45); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: White surface with a hairline border; used for the second action in a pair.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 56px; padding: 14px 26px; border: 1px solid #d8d3c9; border-radius: 20px; background: #ffffff; color: #1b1b1f; font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", sans-serif; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), border-color 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), box-shadow 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #0f9d8c; box-shadow: 0 4px 14px -6px rgba(27, 27, 31, 0.18); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: translateY(0) scale(0.985); }

components.name: Labelled Field
components.description: Label above, input below, helper text underneath explaining what happens.
components.html: The name you used when you set up your account.
components.css: .ds-field { margin: 0 0 18px; } .ds-field label { display: block; margin: 0 0 7px; font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", sans-serif; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; color: #1b1b1f; } .ds-field input { display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 460px; min-height: 56px; padding: 14px 20px; border: 1px solid #d8d3c9; border-radius: 16px; background: #ffffff; color: #1b1b1f; font: 400 17px "DM Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-field input::placeholder { color: rgba(90, 95, 107, 0.6); } .ds-field input:focus { border-color: #0f9d8c; outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.16); } .ds-field .help { display: block; margin: 7px 0 0; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.45; color: #5a5f6b; }

components.name: Camera Panel
components.description: The waiting state - dashed border, face guide, a real button - and the live state with the feed.
components.html:
Camera is off

Look at the camera to switch it on.
components.css: .ds-camera { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 320px; padding: 26px; border-radius: 24px; border: 2px dashed #d8d3c9; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 42%, rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.07), transparent 62%), #f2faf8; text-align: center; } .ds-camera.live { border-style: solid; border-color: #e8e4dc; background: #ffffff; padding: 10px; } .ds-camera h3 { font-family: "Outfit", sans-serif; font-size: 20px; margin: 0; } .ds-camera p { color: #5a5f6b; font-size: 16px; max-width: 34ch; margin: 0; } .ds-guide { width: 150px; height: 190px; border: 2px solid rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.4); border-radius: 50% / 42%; }

components.name: Step Indicator
components.description: Numbered pills with plain-language step names.
components.html:
1. 1 Your details
  2. 2 Your face
components.css: .ds-steps { list-style: none; display: flex; gap: 12px; padding: 0; margin: 0 0 26px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-steps li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 18px 10px 10px; border: 1px solid #e8e4dc; border-radius: 999px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6); font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next", sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: #5a5f6b; } .ds-steps li span { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(27, 27, 31, 0.06); font-family: "Outfit", sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-steps li.active { color: #0b7c6e; border-color: rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.35); background: #e4f6f3; } .ds-steps li.active span { background: #0f9d8c; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: The live-state chip with the one breathing dot in the system.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 999px; background: #e4f6f3; color: #0b7c6e; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-chip .dot { width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%; background: #0f9d8c; animation: ds-breathe 3.5s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-breathe { 0%, 100% { opacity: 0.45; transform: scale(0.94); } 50% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.08); } }

components.name: Reassurance Panel
components.description: The privacy statement that sits wherever a camera or keyboard appears.
components.html: Everything runs on this computer. Your photos and typing samples are stored here and never uploaded.
components.css: .ds-reassure { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 14px; padding: 18px 22px; background: #e4f6f3; border: 1px solid rgba(15, 157, 140, 0.18); border-radius: 20px; color: #0b7c6e; } .ds-reassure p { margin: 0; font-size: 16px; } .ds-reassure strong { display: block; font-size: 16px; }

narrative.overview: ARGUS is a login gate that checks a person's face and their typing rhythm, so the person setting it up may not know what a biometric is, may be on a borrowed laptop, and may be nervous about a camera pointed at them. The console is therefore built as a welcoming desk rather than an instrument panel: warm paper, one friendly teal accent, plain words, generous controls, and the reassurance - repeated where it matters - that photos, typing samples and logs never leave the machine. The one theatrical moment, the verification console, survives as a ritual: the numbers it shows are always the live pipeline's actual output.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, not clinical - cream paper #fffdf9, one soft teal accent, hairline borders instead of hard edges.
Plain language everywhere - no physiological, modality, dwell, clean rounds or FAR in anything a person must read; the technical vocabulary lives behind a link.
Big, forgiving controls - 56px buttons and inputs, sentence-case labels in a low-vision typeface, helper text that says what will happen rather than what is forbidden.
No dead ends - if the camera is off there is always a visible, labelled control to turn it on.
Machine channels stay technical - module codes and identifiers live in 13px monospace where an operator wants them.
The dashed border means waiting - the camera panel and the empty photo slots are the only dashed things in the system.

rules.name: The Plain-Language Rule
rules.body: Anything a person must read is written the way a helpful colleague would say it. Banned in visible copy: physiological, behavioral, modality, normalized, embedding, gallery, cosine similarity, clean rounds, dwell, flight, FAR, FRR, EER, AUC, threshold. These may appear only inside the technical disclosure, where the reader asked for them.

rules.name: The No-Dead-End Rule
rules.body: A screen may never present a sensor that is off without a visible, labelled control that turns it on - in the panel itself, not in a corner. The camera area always shows either a live feed or an instruction and a button; never a grey rectangle.

rules.name: The Reassurance Rule
rules.body: Wherever a camera or a keyboard is involved, the page states that the data stays on the machine. It appears in the footer of every page and beside every capture step.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent. Clay and Rose appear only as verdict colours. Nothing else is coloured for emphasis.

rules.name: The Console Column Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono belongs to machine channels - identifiers, module codes, lab readouts. It is never used for an instruction, a label a person acts on, or a sentence.

rules.name: The 15px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text a person must read is smaller than 15px. Technical mono may be 13px.

rules.name: The Porcelain Rule
rules.body: Blur belongs to fixed chrome (nav, toasts). Scrolling content never carries backdrop-filter. Depth is hairline + soft shadow + inset - never a dark offset drop-shadow costume, and never a glow on a non-live element.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Waiting Rule
rules.body: A dashed border is reserved for an element that is waiting for the person - the camera panel, the empty photo slots. Solid hairlines mean ready.

dos: Do write instructions as a helpful colleague would: what happens, what to do, what if it goes wrong.
Do put a visible, labelled control next to anything that can be off.
Do say where the data goes (nowhere) whenever a camera or keyboard is involved.
Do keep the technical numbers behind a disclosure, and state the plain answer first.
Do animate transform and opacity only; --ease cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) for UI, --ease-io for the breathing dot.
Do keep tap targets at least 48px and text at least 15px.
Do treat reduced-motion as global: the stylesheet collapses all animation/transition to 0.01ms.
Do self-host every asset - the CSP is default-src 'self' with no inline style or script; page config rides the #bio-config JSON block.
donts: Don't use jargon in anything a person must read (The Plain-Language Rule).
Don't name things in all-caps mono labels or module codes - that is the operator's language, not the user's.
Don't show a sensor that is off without a button to turn it on (The No-Dead-End Rule).
Don't use mix-blend-mode: screen on a light surface; use multiply.
Don't use backdrop-blur on scrolling content; fixed chrome only.
Don't animate width/height/top/left - bars fill with scaleX, strips with scaleY.
Don't introduce a second accent, or colour something for emphasis.
Don't hard-code raster font links, inline styles, or inline scripts.
